description: Advanced computability, parsing, language classes and complexity concepts.

questions.questionText: What is a recursive enumerable language?
questions.optionB: A language recognized by some Turing Machine
questions.explanation: Recursively enumerable languages are recognizable by Turing machines.

questions.questionText: What is the complement of a decidable language?
questions.explanation: Decidable languages are closed under complement.

questions.questionText: Are decidable languages closed under union?
questions.explanation: Decidable languages are closed under union.

questions.questionText: Are decidable languages closed under intersection?
questions.explanation: Decidable languages are closed under intersection.

questions.questionText: Are recursively enumerable languages closed under union?
questions.explanation: RE languages are closed under union.

questions.questionText: Are recursively enumerable languages closed under complement?
questions.explanation: RE languages are not closed under complement in general.

questions.questionText: What is a configuration of a PDA?
questions.optionB: A description of its current state, input position and stack
questions.explanation: A PDA configuration records state, remaining input and stack contents.

questions.questionText: What is a sentential form?
questions.optionA: A string of terminals and nonterminals derived from the start symbol
questions.explanation: A sentential form may contain both terminals and nonterminals.

questions.questionText: What is left recursion in grammar?
questions.optionD: A nonterminal can derive a string beginning with itself
questions.explanation: Left recursion occurs when a nonterminal can derive a sentential form beginning with itself.

questions.questionText: Why is ambiguity important in parsing?
questions.optionD: A string may have multiple structural interpretations
questions.explanation: Ambiguity can give multiple parse structures for the same string.

questions.questionText: Which grammar form is useful for CYK parsing?
questions.explanation: CYK parsing is typically applied to grammars in Chomsky Normal Form.

questions.questionText: What is CYK?
questions.optionB: A parsing algorithm for CFGs in CNF
questions.explanation: CYK is a dynamic programming algorithm for CFG parsing in CNF.

questions.questionText: What is Earley parsing used for?
questions.explanation: Earley parsing is a general CFG parsing algorithm.

questions.questionText: What is a universal language?
questions.optionA: A language describing acceptance of encoded machines and inputs
questions.explanation: A universal language can encode machine-input pairs and their acceptance behavior.

questions.questionText: What is diagonalization used for in computability theory?
questions.optionB: Proving certain problems are not computable/decidable
questions.explanation: Diagonalization is a major technique for proving non-computability.

questions.questionText: What is a configuration in a Turing Machine?
questions.optionD: Current state, tape contents and head position
questions.explanation: A TM configuration describes the complete current computational situation.

questions.questionText: What is a semi-decision procedure?
questions.optionB: It halts and accepts yes-instances but may loop on no-instances
questions.optionD: It always halts with no answer
questions.explanation: A recognizer may halt and accept members but need not halt on non-members.

questions.questionText: What is a decidable set?
questions.optionC: A set whose membership can be decided by a halting algorithm
questions.explanation: Decidable sets have effective membership algorithms that halt.

questions.questionText: Which theorem helps characterize regular languages through distinguishability?
questions.explanation: Myhill-Nerode characterizes regular languages using distinguishable equivalence classes.

questions.questionText: What is a recursive function in classical computability theory?
questions.optionC: Only a recursive program in C
questions.optionD: A computable function in the recursive-function framework
questions.explanation: Recursive functions form a classical formalization of computable functions.

questions.questionText: What does PSPACE refer to?
questions.explanation: PSPACE contains problems solvable with polynomial amount of memory.

questions.questionText: What does P commonly denote in complexity theory?
questions.optionA: Problems solvable in polynomial time by a deterministic machine
questions.explanation: P is the class of decision problems solvable in polynomial time by deterministic algorithms.

questions.questionText: What does NP commonly denote?
questions.optionC: Problems whose solutions can be verified in polynomial time
questions.explanation: NP is commonly characterized by polynomial-time verifiability of certificates.

questions.questionText: What is a polynomial-time reduction used for?
questions.explanation: Polynomial-time reductions relate problems while controlling transformation complexity.

questions.questionText: What is the purpose of complexity theory?
questions.optionD: Study resources required to solve computational problems
questions.explanation: Complexity theory studies computational resources such as time and space.
